info.bio: Doctor Paul Bruce Dickinson, nacido el 7 de agosto de 1958 en Worksop Notts, Inglaterra es el vocalista principal en la banda de heavy metal Iron Maiden que entró para sustituir a Paul Di'Anno en 1982. Hasta antes de unirse a ellos en 1982 para grabar The Number of the Beast, fue el cantante de Samson. Pero sus comienzos en la música se remontan a su época con Styx en 1976, de ahí pasó a cantar en Speed desde 1977 a 1978 y cuando este grupo se separó se unió a Shots hasta el verano de 1979.

scenes.name: Iron Maiden
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: La gran triunfadora de la NWOBHM y la banda que más saca del Apocalipsis («The Number of the Beast») y de la literatura gótica («Murders in the Rue Morgue», tomada casi literalmente de Poe). Sus letras recorren todo el registro del caos: asesinos y carnicerías («Killers», «Genghis Khan»), injusticia («Only the Good Die Young»), los indios perseguidos de «Run to the Hills», la alienación de «Stranger in a Strange Land» y la locura de «Sea of Madness»; y su prostituta de «22 Acacia Avenue» es ejemplo del papel de la mujer en el heavy. Sus innovaciones rítmicas influyen en el thrash.

scenes.name: El oficio: del air guitar al dios del metal
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: El músico de heavy sale del público: es el fan que toca la guitarra de aire en el concierto de UFO de 1979 y quiere estar donde está Michael Schenker. No hay escuela ni beca: hace falta talento musical y dramático (actuar la emoción por trescientas veces), un cuerpo joven y atlético (correr y pesas en la gira, el pelo largo como signo de autenticidad) y aprender a vivir en un grupo que no es ni familia ni oficina, con sus «problemas de ego» por la rivalidad entre cantante y guitarrista. El heavy es el estilo más caro de montar y casi no hay clubes donde empezar; el código exige temas propios y autenticidad. Firmar con un sello convierte a la banda en una empresa del capitalismo tardío frente a un oligopolio. El ciclo es componer, grabar (paciencia; el primer disco de Black Sabbath se hizo en doce horas, Spreading the Disease de Anthrax en cinco meses) y girar (aguante: esperar, esperar). La recompensa no es el dinero sino el carisma del chamán que alcanza el éxtasis dionisíaco ante miles de personas; el precio, «quemarse o apagarse», porque nadie que viva lo bastante puede cumplir el código.

scenes.name: La «muerte» del metal en los noventa
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: A mediados de los noventa se expide el certificado de defunción del metal, y hay varios sospechosos. Para los headbangers fue una puñalada de Metallica: el disco homónimo de 1991, lleno de baladas radiables, Load y ReLoad, el cartel de Lollapalooza y la portada de Rolling Stone con pelo corto, eyeliner y piercings. Otros culpan al grunge, que destrona al lite metal justo cuando Skid Row, Mötley Crüe, Van Halen y Guns N’ Roses debutaban en el número uno en 1991. Pero los grandes grupos también se oxidan: Black Sabbath lleva quince años de cambios de cantante (Dehumanizer con Dio en 1992 y luego solo queda Tony Iommi), Ozzy anuncia que se retira y se desretira, Judas Priest queda inerte tras Painkiller cuando Halford se marcha a Fight y lo ven como un Judas, Bruce Dickinson deja Iron Maiden en 1993. Los fans se consuelan con bandas tributo y discos de homenaje (Nativity in Black, 1994), y el último clavo del ataúd es el disco de versiones melódicas de Pat Boone, In a Metal Mood.

scenes.name: La bestia ha vuelto: OzzFest y las reuniones
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: A finales de siglo el metal vuelve a la corriente principal. Con el alternativo moribundo y la electrónica sin despegar, el público fiel sigue ahí: tres mil personas esperan cinco horas en un centro comercial de Chicago en 1998 a que Black Sabbath les firme discos. El detonante es el OzzFest de 1997, organizado por la mánager de Ozzy, que vende más que Lollapalooza con Pantera, Machine Head, Fear Factory, Type O Negative, Neurosis, tres cuartas partes de Black Sabbath y Marilyn Manson, cuyas provocaciones atraen protestas cristianas y titulares. Metallica vuelve a tocar su thrash en directo y en Garage Inc.; Judas Priest ficha a Tim «Ripper» Owens, cantante de una banda tributo llamada British Steel; Mötley Crüe recupera a Vince Neil, Kiss se reúne en 1998, Dickinson regresa a Iron Maiden y Black Sabbath hace en 1999 una gira de reunión con disco de oro. Weinstein ve en ese regreso el gusto «prole» de la cultura de fin de siglo, un contrapeso a la feminización del pop y la ansiedad milenarista: la bestia se niega a morir.

podcast.title: Certified Airline Pilot and Aviation Entrepreneur
podcast.body: Bruce Dickinson is a certified airline pilot who learned to fly in Florida in the 1990s. He has flown 757s for the now-defunct airline Astrayus and is qualified to pilot 737s and the large 747-400. He personally flies Iron Maiden's chartered planes for their world tours and owns his own charter airline and aviation company based in Cardiff, Wales. For recreation, he also flies a Fokker triplane, participating in reenactments of famous World War I battles at air shows. "He's now qualified to fly 737s and a 747-400 which is one huge aircraft."

He has flown for several airlines, including Astraeus, where he piloted 757s, and is now qualified to fly 737s and the large 747-400. He personally flies Iron Maiden's chartered planes during their world tours and owns his own charter airline and aviation company based in Cardiff, Wales. podcast.title: Commercial Airline Pilot
podcast.body: During a break from Iron Maiden, Bruce Dickinson obtained his commercial airline pilot's license. He is rated to fly Boeing 747s and has served as the captain of "Ed Force One," Iron Maiden's chartered jet used for touring. "When Bruce Dickinson took a break from Iron Maiden, he got his commercial airline pilot's license. He's rated to fly 747s and sometimes does."

xref.title: Bruce Dickinson's Commercial Aviation Career
xref.body: Bruce Dickinson, the singer for the metal band Iron Maiden, is a full-fledged pilot for a UK charter airline, flying 757s. He was originally taught to fly by a British Airways pilot. In 2008, during a 7-week World Tour, Bruce personally flew the plane that transported the band and crew between continents and gigs. "Bruce flies there's 757s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Chris Sangerides as Producer for Fully Completely
xref.body: Chris Sangerides, a Greek Cypriot, was chosen to produce *Fully Completely*. He was known for his work with heavy metal acts like Judas Priest, Black Sabbath, Ozzy, and Thin Lizzy, but The Tragically Hip were primarily drawn to the sound of records he produced for Concrete Blonde. The band felt disarmed by his lovely demeanor, and he showed his enthusiasm by traveling to Toronto to see them play at the Horseshoe Tavern before recording. Sangerides implemented a traditional 1970s recording technique, which was "completely alien" to the band's usual live-style approach, focusing on building tracks from the bass and drums upwards. "In my recollection, it was our idea to work with Chris, but in retrospect, I think Bruce Dickinson was very good at putting an idea out there and making you think that it was your own."

xref.body: Bruce Dickinson's passion for airplanes led him to become a fully qualified airline pilot, rated to fly Boeing 747s. He further channeled this interest into business by running his own aircraft maintenance and pilot training facility, Cardiff Aviation. "he's now a fully qualified airline pilot, rated to fly 747s."

xref.title: Record Deal with MCA Records
xref.body: The band's debut EP, which served as their calling card, brought them to the attention of Bruce Dickinson, the newly appointed president of MCA Records. Dickinson was tipped off by a song he heard on a compilation CD. He flew to Toronto from New York and was impressed by a two-song set the band performed at Massey Hall, leading to their record deal and the reissue of their debut EP. "This is how they came to the attention of Bruce Dickinson, the brand new president of MCA Records."

xref.title: Seven Lead Singers; Paul Di'Anno on First Two Albums; Bruce Dickinson Returned After Blaze Bayley's Vocal Issues
xref.body: Iron Maiden's singer history begins with Paul Day (about two years), then Dennis Wilcock (a performer who would put fake blood capsules in his mouth and draw a sword across his face to "bleed" on stage), then Paul Di'Anno — who recorded the band's first two studio albums before being fired for excessive drinking and drug use. Bruce Dickinson joined in 1981 and was with the band through 1993 before leaving to focus on solo work. Blaze Bayley replaced him but ran into serious vocal difficulties; when Dickinson indicated he wanted to return in 1999, Bayley was out and Dickinson returned, remaining to the present. "Dennis Wilcock had a thing about where he'd put capsules of fake blood in his mouth."
